resources.string: Finds the Linux Lab window on the screen so that your touches on it can be sent straight to the Linux desktop as real touches. It reads nothing but the position of windows.
Your touches go to Linux as on a touchscreen.
The screen works as a touchpad for Linux.
Open it, and touches will work by themselves.
It is switched on in the Android settings, under Developer options.
So that the helper finds the Linux Lab window. In the list, open Linux Lab Helper and turn it on.
Open the app info, the three-dot menu, \"Allow restricted settings\". Then press \"Turn on\" again.
This is how your touches get to Linux. In the list, choose Linux Lab Helper.
Once, in the terminal of Linux Lab.
Linux has no touch module any more. Install it again.
Takes a few seconds. Programs open in Linux are closed.
The full Ubuntu 26.04 desktop with GNOME is not installed yet.
This version of the helper brings fixes for the Ubuntu desktop. Updating it takes a few minutes and needs the internet; open programs keep running until Linux Lab is restarted.
Android asks before it installs the update; your settings stay.
Allow Linux Lab Helper to install apps, then tap Update again.
Every finger touches Linux, as on a phone.
A finger moves the pointer, a tap clicks, a two-finger tap is a right click.
Android or Linux: chosen in the settings of Linux Lab. With GNOME the Android keyboard types in any language.
Add the \"Touchpad\" tile to quick settings
Remove the touch module from Linux
Done once, in the terminal of Linux Lab.
A desktop like on a computer, with everything it needs on a tablet, and touches. About 20 minutes, needs Wi-Fi and 6 GB.
The desktop of Linux Lab stays as it is. A few seconds.
Now run it in Linux Lab.
Open Linux Lab, and a terminal in it
The terminal icon is on the panel and in the list of programs.
Paste the command and press Enter
Paste with the clipboard button of the Android keyboard or with Ctrl+Shift+V.
About 20 minutes. Keep Linux Lab open; the terminal may be closed, the installation goes on.
Wait for the update to finish
A few minutes. The terminal can be closed, the update goes on.
Close Linux Lab and open it again
It starts with the Ubuntu desktop.
The module is not loaded any more.
The fixes work from then on, the desktop stays the one you chose.
The way Linux Lab works by itself. chroot is several times faster, and needs root.
Without proot: files, installing and building are several times faster. Needs root on every start of Linux Lab.
chroot needs root: KernelSU, Magisk or APatch.
Give root to Linux Lab Helper in KernelSU, Magisk or APatch, then tap chroot again.
chroot is chosen, but the root service did not answer: Linux runs under proot.
the root service did not start
